_note: Recurring-series programming for RetroVision (channels/publish.php). Five real Internet Archive-backed shows (see series/retro-*/series.json for exact discovery queries/collections and per-episode editorial review) tile a wall-to-wall 24-hour day, each show airing in two separate dayparts with its own independent sequential rotation cursor (same pattern channels/science already established for its 12-show lineup): a 6-hour overnight deep-dive block for The Computer Chronicles (retro-technology, the largest and longest-running single show in the catalog) plus nine 2-hour blocks, one per remaining daypart. Every block opts into multi-episode packing (packing.enabled, mode sequential, on_unfit defer) so a slot plays as many complete, approved episodes back-to-back as actually fit, instead of exactly one -- these are short archival films/TV episodes (49s-30min), not hour-long shows. boundary.mode is hard on every block: across the whole approved catalog the longest single approved episode is 1790s (Industrial America) / 1776s (Computer Chronicles), both comfortably under even the shortest (7200s) slot, so no block has ever actually needed to run over.
